title: Brass and Palms

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The Grand Hotel: brass, palms, and a concierge who has never heard of anyone. Especially anyone you ask about.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: The concierge owes me a favor — na ja, three favors. You're volunteering for lost property. Match the luggage, earn the register.

caseLine: Two names to place under one roof: Casal, and Adele's 'Dr. Lorentz'.

title: Casal Holds Court

lines.speaker: casal
lines.en: I sell beautiful things to people who deserve worse. That is not theft, detective — it's ecology.

lines.speaker: casal
lines.en: Search my shop. Please. Loudly, in front of witnesses. Innocence is wasted if nobody watches it.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Half this shop is honest. Guess which half.

caseLine: Casal insists on being searched — theatrically. Take him up on it literally.

peopleFacts.fact: Offers his shop ostentatiously. Outrage on retainer.

flavorChoice.warm: Beautiful things deserve honest paperwork, Mr. Casal.

title: The Die Doesn't Match

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: The nicked serif clears him of the crate — and the deciphered ledger convicts him of the acquaintance. He has dealt with 'Nachtigall' before.

lines.speaker: casal
lines.en: I never met them. One does not meet a voice. One receives it.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: His outrage goes quiet and real. He stops performing. It is somehow worse.

caseLine: The customs stamp is a forgery — Casal's mark, not his die. But his ledger knows the bird's name.

peopleFacts.fact: Cleared of the theft; guilty of much else. Prior Nachtigall lots.

title: The Veiled Woman

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: Don't look. Grey gloves, eleven o'clock. Walks like unpaid rent.

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Veiled, unhurried, she leaves a note at the desk, tips the bell-boy exactly right, and crosses the lobby like she owns the marble.

caseLine: A veiled woman leaves Casal's summonses. Sigil: the Lattice Stall. Day: Friday.

peopleFacts.fact: A woman: veiled, grey gloves, tips exactly right.

title: Already Searched

lines.speaker: narration
lines.en: Suite 412, searched before you — tidily. The false drawer's sticking panel kept its secret: LATTICE STALL. FRIDAY. BRING THE 1926 FILE. — NACHTIGALL.

lines.speaker: casal
lines.en: They wanted my file. The 1926 file. I keep it — elsewhere.

lines.speaker: margo
lines.en: The market is my quarter, Halloway. Friday you're my guest — eyes open, mouth shut, and smile.

caseLine: Nachtigall summons Casal to the Lattice Stall, Friday, with the 1926 file.

peopleFacts.fact: Wants the 1926 file — the sale's paper trail.
